blocks.text: Menahem’s payment to Pul should not be treated as generic tribute whose meaning is self-evident. Tribute could follow defeat, express strategic submission, purchase support, or restore a vassal relationship. Here the text gives the payment a specific function: Menahem seeks Assyrian support to secure his hold on the kingdom and raises the silver from Israel’s wealthy men. The payment alone does not disclose every motive, so its purpose should be interpreted from this account rather than from a single model of tribute.

The capture and deportation in verse 29 belongs to a staged reduction of Israel, not one event that should absorb every later Assyrian action. Tiglath-pileser’s annexations, Shalmaneser’s siege, Sargon’s conquest claims, the revolt of 720 BCE, and later resettlements cannot be compressed into a single securely dated operation. Second Kings itself distributes territorial loss, siege, deportation, and incoming resettlement across separate notices, so this verse should be read as one stage in that sequence.
